tools.name: get_user_by_username
tools.description: Look up a Twitter/X user profile by username (handle). Returns the profile including follower and following counts. Bills one user request against the caller's balance.

tools.name: get_user_by_id
tools.description: Look up a Twitter/X user profile by numeric user ID. Bills one user request against the caller's balance.

tools.name: search_users
tools.description: Search Twitter/X user profiles by name or handle. Returns one page of matching profiles and bills against the caller's balance. Use this when you know roughly who someone is but not their exact handle.

tools.name: get_tweet
tools.description: Fetch a single Twitter/X post by its numeric ID, including engagement counts. Bills one post request against the caller's balance.

tools.name: get_tweet_thread
tools.description: Fetch one page of a Twitter/X thread — the chain of follow-up posts the author wrote under their own post ("1/", "2/", ...). Give it the ID of any post in the chain and it returns that chain in order. It does NOT return what other people replied; use get_tweet_comments for those. A post the author n

tools.name: get_tweet_comments
tools.description: Fetch one page of replies to a Twitter/X post. Returns about 20 replies plus a next_cursor. The first item of a page can repeat the last item of the previous page, so de-duplicate by post id when paging. Each call bills against the caller's balance — do not page through the whole conversation unless

tools.name: get_user_tweets
tools.description: Fetch one page of a user's own posts (excluding replies), newest first. Returns about 20 posts plus a next_cursor. If the account has a pinned post it is prepended to every page, so de-duplicate by post id when paging. Each call bills against the caller's balance — do not page through a whole timeli

tools.name: get_user_tweets_and_replies
tools.description: Fetch one page of a user's posts including their replies, newest first. Returns about 20 items plus a next_cursor. If the account has a pinned post it is prepended to every page, so de-duplicate by post id when paging. Each call bills against the caller's balance. Requires a numeric user ID: call ge

tools.name: get_user_mentions
tools.description: Fetch one page of posts mentioning a given user, newest first. Returns about 20 posts plus a next_cursor. The first item of a page can repeat the last item of the previous page, so de-duplicate by post id when paging. Each call bills against the caller's balance.

tools.name: get_user_followers
tools.description: Fetch one page of a user's followers. This is one of the most expensive tools: a page is set upstream and can run to ~100 user records, every one of which is billed. Never page through a large account's followers without the user explicitly asking. Requires a numeric user ID.

tools.name: get_user_following
tools.description: Fetch one page of the accounts a user follows. Expensive: a page is set upstream and can run to ~100 user records, every one of which is billed. Never page through a large account's following list without the user explicitly asking. Requires a numeric user ID.

tools.name: check_is_following
tools.description: Check whether one Twitter/X user follows another. Far cheaper than fetching a follower list — use this whenever the question is about a specific pair of accounts. Both IDs must be numeric.

tools.name: search_tweets
tools.description:
Search Twitter/X posts. Returns one page of about 20 results plus a
next_cursor, and bills one search request against the caller's balance.

The query supports Twitter's advanced search operators, and using them is
almost always better than a bare keyword search:
  from:handle          posts by an a

tools.name: get_list_tweets
tools.description: Fetch one page of posts from a Twitter/X list, newest first. A page is large — around 100 posts — plus a next_cursor. Billing is per result, so one call here costs several times a single-user timeline call; do not page through a busy list unless the user asked for that.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_tweet, get_tweet_thread, get_tweet_comments, get_user_tweets, get_user_tweets_and_replies, get_user_mentions, search_tweets, get_list_tweets · Private data: get_user_followers, get_user_following · Public sink: get_tweet, get_tweet_thread, get_tweet_comments, get_user_tweets, get_user_tweets_and_replies, get_user_mentions · Destructive: get_user_followers, get_user_following.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_tweet, get_tweet_thread, get_tweet_comments, get_user_tweets, get_user_tweets_and_replies, get_user_mentions, search_tweets, get_list_tweets · Private data: get_user_followers, get_user_following · Public sink: get_tweet, get_tweet_thread, get_tweet_comments, get_user_tweets, get_user_tweets_and_replies, get_user_mentions · Destructive: get_user_followers, get_user_following

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
